purpose: Attempt bounded prestarted, single-use advisory JVMs after the fresh Tier-1 experiment failed. No worker processes a second private request.

scope.baseline: 4 vCPU / 8 GiB; workstation screening is not target-host acceptance.
scope.first_implementation: Isolated copied installation and disabled production adapter, after exact six-seat council approval and two matching clean Lean builds. The live preview remains fresh DEFAULT until every promotion gate passes.
scope.operations: Only DocumentQueries advisory VALIDATE may use the pool. Durable validation, revalidation and solver jobs retain fresh DEFAULT execution and their existing worker permits.
excluded: Synthetic Alloy parsing or JIT training before READY

authorization_order: Complete concrete image, containment, protocol and lifecycle design; freeze this contract, experiment, model, exact types, verifiers, source anchors and feasibility evidence.
Obtain two GPT-6.1 Terra, two GPT-6.1 Sol and two GPT-6 Astra reviews for the exact input root; reconcile blocking findings before dependent production edits.
Run the registered model verifier with two isolated clean builds, exact elaborated types/axioms, witnesses and matching deterministic artifacts.

Implement only the approved bounded candidate. Freeze implementation, runtime fixtures, verifiers and toolchain before finite safety/differential execution. Formal model verification does not establish Java/OS correspondence.

Run performance only after the finite safety and differential prerequisites pass. Keep all failures; no selection or live activation unless every mandatory promotion gate passes. A material contract deviation requires new proof/review before dependent edits.

amendments.context_cleanup: For this disabled advisory candidate only, replace the literal no-Alloy-launch-before-CLEAN ordering in spec/document-context-cleanup.json with no-private-model-byte-before-CLEAN. A standby may initialize only fixed trusted bootstrap classes before a request exists. Fresh scoped context must still complete all existing full-history checks, close its SQL connection and obtain exact generation/nonce-bound CLEAN with successPermitted=true before any private frame is sent. Existing context failure/UNKNOWN behavior is unchanged.
amendments.image_descriptor_budget: The planning contract's provisional 64-descriptor cap is replaced by a measured maximum of 512 image files/descriptors, while retaining a 64 MiB aggregate image byte cap. This preserves directory/classpath layout without introducing JAR packaging. Actual inventory must fit before implementation execution; no silent cap increase.
amendments.delegation: Unlike the old fresh Tier-1 experiment's Delegate=no wrapper, this new candidate requires a private user-owned delegated cgroup subtree, verified before launching Allow. Do not change host AppArmor, sysctls, privileges or system services. Unsupported delegation disables pooling; no uncontained fallback.
amendments.image_setup_file_limit: Sealed-memory capture and bwrap --ro-bind-data copy the21MiB Alloy JAR, so the trusted helper and namespace setup require FS64MiB. Keep AS2GiB and per-process CPU12s from helper startup. Mount the fixed pinned /usr/bin/prlimit read-only into the sandbox and execute it to lower BOTH hard and soft FS limits to8MiB before the JVM starts. No private model bytes are sent until READY and runtime evidence confirms final limits. This replaces only the setup ordering, not the untrusted worker limit. Installed --ro-bind-fd cannot mount anonymous memfds here; retain failed probes.

fixed_budgets.limits_note: Trusted helper applies AS2GiB, CPU12s, FS64MiB and finite FD1024 limits before image capture; namespace setup retains them. The fixed in-sandbox prlimit lowers hard+soft FS to8MiB before Java starts. Java Xmx512m/Xss512k/SerialGC/ActiveProcessorCount2/metaspace128m/classspace64m/codecache48m remain. CPU12s is PER-PROCESS RLIMIT_CPU, not an aggregate tree ceiling; JVM accounting includes bootstrap, while whole-group cpu.stat includes every helper/refill. A slot denotes one contained process tree, including helpers/bwrap.
fixed_budgets.image_descriptor_note: 512 caps image descriptors only; actual process FD limits must leave measured room for stdio/control/cgroup/bwrap descriptors. Pin and check an adequate finite RLIMIT_NOFILE (initial1024) before capture; failure is unsupported, not an implicit cap increase.

immutable_image.adapter: A fixed installed Python3 helper creates one sealable memfd per actual classes/resource file, dependency .jar and solver/alloy.jar. It streams at most64MiB total and512files, requires normalized relative paths and ordinary non-symlink files, rejects duplicate destinations and unexpected tree members, adds F_SEAL_WRITE/GROW/SHRINK/SEAL and verifies seals. No private model input is available to the helper during capture.
immutable_image.identity: Capture exact sorted logical path + NUL + file bytes + NUL, then exact java.runtime.version, matching current BuildIdentity. Compare the aggregate captured-byte identity to the parent-pinned full build and independently check the Alloy SHA6037cbeee0e8423c1c468447ed10f5fcf2f2743a2ffc39cb1c81f2905c0fdb9d. Inventory and cap violations fail before READY. Seal checks and mounted-byte equality require actual runtime evidence.
immutable_image.mounts: Pass only sealed descriptors to exec(prlimit,bwrap); bwrap --ro-bind-data copies their immutable contents into read-only mounts at existing /app/classes, /app/dependency and /app/solver.jar paths under trusted setup FS64MiB. Add exactly one fixed read-only system executable mount /usr/bin/prlimit. Execute /usr/bin/prlimit --fsize=8388608 -- <existing Java command> inside the sandbox, lowering hard+soft FS before Java. Preserve classpath /app/classes:/app/solver.jar:/app/dependency/* and resource names. No JAR packaging or compiler optimization. Test exact mount bytes, application classpath and final process limits. Helper closes every descriptor on failure; bwrap consumes sealed descriptor ownership on exec.
immutable_image.runtime_tcb: JDK, native libraries, /etc/java-17-openjdk, Python interpreter/stdlib, helper and bwrap/prlimit remain trusted installed runtime components, pinned in experimental manifests. Application executable bytes are copied/sealed; read-only host mounts alone are not claimed immutable. Host administrators and same-principal executable tampering remain outside this candidate's adversary model.
immutable_image.use_fences: Retain current full BuildIdentity construction and launch scans plus Alloy pin. For pooled use add full installed BuildIdentity/Alloy checks immediately before private handoff and after owned cleanup before publication; the latter is a NEW fence and measured cost, not a claim about current DocumentQueries. A change permanently disables the pool incarnation and retires every standby. Never cache or substitute a JAR-only identity. Only an OBSERVED mismatch triggers incarnation disable; no continuous host filesystem monitoring or atomicity with arbitrary external writes is claimed. The final scan is performed by the publication method, never accepted as a cached earlier boolean. Sealed application bytes remain stable independently.

ownership.ledger: One synchronized owner mutates a bounded two-slot ledger. Persist complete generation-bound state using private0600 atomic replacement, fsync and directory fsync before spawning; hold an exclusive private0700 pool lock. Capture server boot_id/PID/start, pool incarnation, slot monotone generation, random nonce, cgroup path+inode and expected image/policy. Reservation occurs before spawn. No unsigned Java semaphore release can stand in for process cleanup. Journal schema is closed and contains only operational identity, phase, counters and cleanup metadata; never candidate source, inventory, context, private response, authentication token or database credentials. Completed worker, reader/writer future and staged lease references are detached after terminal release; reusable coordinator state must not retain model frames.
ownership.join_barrier: Create and open the exact empty worker cgroup before ProcessBuilder starts the fixed helper. Direct child first arms parent-death SIGKILL and verifies expected parent incarnation, then waits for a bounded PUBLIC bootstrap descriptor. Parent captures and persists child PID/start before releasing this barrier. Helper validates its own and parent's identity, cgroup identity and owner generation, joins that cgroup, verifies membership, then captures images and execs prlimit/bwrap. No child forks or runs application code before joining. Helper disappearance or pre-join uncertainty still requires direct-child reap.
ownership.containment: Retain --unshare-all, --new-session, --die-with-parent, --cap-drop ALL, clear environment and existing system read-only mounts/tmpfs/proc/dev. The private worker cgroup is not mounted into the worker sandbox. Keep FD-backed cgroup.events/cgroup.kill ownership for exact generation; do not kill arbitrary PIDs or reused paths. Verify all process ancestry and membership during registered tests.
ownership.cleanup: Stop input, mark generation retiring/poisoned, request cgroup.kill and exact owned direct-child destruction, then wait for direct child reaping and positive populated=0 on the captured group. Close all stream/task/image/control descriptors and record terminal counters before removing the group. Only then persist terminal cleanup and release once. Missing group, timeout, unreadable state or ambiguous ancestry is UNKNOWN and retains the slot; elapsed time never proves absence.
ownership.restart: A successor must acquire the pool lock and reconcile every persisted reservation before admitting work. Only exact prior group identity plus observed empty state and old direct-child absence permits release. Never clear a pre-key/spawn-uncertain record merely because its PID is missing. Unsupported or incomplete reconciliation keeps the pool disabled; operator reset is not an automatic success path.
ownership.shared_capacity: The existing active-operation permit remains1. A new shared live-tree ledger covers every warm worker and every fresh DocumentWorker/ProcessRunner launch when pooling is enabled. Fresh operations may coexist with at most one standby; all STARTING/READY/BUSY/RETIRING/UNKNOWN reservations count toward2. The disabled path retains current fresh behavior. An enabled incarnation with unknown cleanup never switches itself back to the fresh uncontained path; it stays unavailable until mechanically reconciled. Disabled DEFAULT is a separate server-start policy. Every enabled-mode fresh solver/durable/revalidation launch uses the same gated helper join, generation-owned child cgroup and exact cleanup receipt; it executes its ordinary fresh DEFAULT entrypoint without READY/prewarming. Keeping flags/semantics does not mean keeping the uncontained launch topology. Test both worker kinds together, including lingering descendants. Bridge/SQL helper processes remain in the control leaf and are not JVM-worker slots; the existing active-operation permit bounds their concurrent use.

protocol.entrypoint: New fixed WarmDocumentWorkerMain redirects library stdout to stderr before initialization. Bootstrap is exactly JsonWire encode/decode of public UTF-8 {} and Class.forName with initialization of dev.allow.document.DocumentEngine and edu.mit.csail.sdg.parser.CompUtil using the same application loader. No source parsing, solving, user data or corpus preloading. It emits exactly one ASCII line ALLOW-WARM-1 <generation-nonce> <image-sha256> followed by LF, then accepts one bounded VALIDATE frame through the existing document engine. REVALIDATE and unknown operations are rejected. Freeze the complete loaded application/resource inventory and initialization outcomes in runtime evidence; do not silently expand the warmup.
protocol.parent: One transport owner continuously drains bounded stderr and stdout from launch through EOF. The sole stdout reader has explicit STARTUP, IDLE and REQUEST phases: parse exactly one READY line<=256bytes under startup deadline, reject any further byte during IDLE, then capture the single bounded response in REQUEST. Validate nonce/image/phase/ownership before advertising READY. Atomically transition to REQUEST when consuming the exact context permit before any private write. Do not transfer buffered streams to FrameProcess or create a competing reader. Whole-life stderr limit32768 includes startup/idle/request. READY alone is not image or OS safety evidence.
protocol.request: Exactly one existing protocol1 VALIDATE frame with fresh requestId; no second frame or request. Input serialization occurs after fresh context. Stdin closes after the one frame. Preserve complete response limits, field checks, nonce equality, exitCode0 and full semantic result. Additional READY/response lines, late/oversized/truncated output or stderr overflow poison the generation.
protocol.publication: Stage the full private response. Require exact identity, noncancelled generation, unexpired total request deadline, direct-child reap, owned-group empty, full final installed-build/Alloy fence, then atomically publish while still holding the active-operation permit. Cancellation linearized before publication suppresses the reply even if validation succeeded. No advisory state authorizes persistence. The pool returns an owned staged-result lease, not an already-published reply. DocumentQueries builds the unchanged public envelope while the lease and active-operation permit remain held; the lease publication method performs the final fence/deadline/cancellation check and linearizes publication immediately before returning those bytes. Close-without-publish poisons/cleans/releases as appropriate. Internal caller interruption and service shutdown are cancellation sources; this adds no public cancellation endpoint. A cancellation after the defined publication point cannot retract already returned bytes.
protocol.context_adapter: The SQL CLEAN receipt remains private to the existing Python CLI/proxy protocol. Java does not invent or infer that receipt. DocumentGateway continues to check its private response nonce and the CLI returns context only after exact proxy/lease generation, nonce, CLEAN and successPermitted checks. A package-private single-use context permit is created only on successful DocumentValidationContext.read for the current admitted operation; it binds a server-created operation nonce, exact draft request hash, document/base revision and current policy. The pool consumes this permit exactly once at handoff. Never accept a permit or cleanup flag from browser JSON. The model receipt represents this trusted adapter composition; it is not a new public authority field or a Java proof of PostgreSQL absence. Permit also binds expected build and pool incarnation; replayed, mismatched and stale permits are rejected before writing.

bootstrap_schema.transport: Exactly one UTF-8 JSON line<=4096bytes on direct-child stdin, followed later by one private frame only after helper exec, verified READY and fresh context permit. Helper reads one byte at a time through LF with no read-ahead; reject duplicate/unknown/missing fields, invalid types and NULs. The trusted parent transport owns all writes and sends nothing further until those gates. The helper cannot prove that no future pipe byte will arrive; phase-violation tests target the parent authority boundary, not an impossible pipe-absence proof. Helper emits no stdout; only Java emits READY.

fields.cgroupRoot: absolute private delegated root supplied by the trusted launcher

bootstrap_schema.path_and_fd_ownership: The helper receives expected owner identity and root identity as fixed launcher argv as well, rejects bootstrap mismatches, opens root and each relative cgroup directory with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and validates fstat device/inode before descriptor-relative access to cgroup.procs. Reject dot/dotdot/separators in generated components and symlinked target roots. Parent retains its independently opened group descriptors. Helper closes cgroup/control descriptors before exec; only stdin/stdout/stderr and enumerated sealed image descriptors survive into bwrap, which consumes image descriptors. Check actual inherited FD inventory; unexpected descriptors block runtime acceptance.
bootstrap_schema.failure: Any parse/identity/path/join/seal/cap/exec failure exits with no READY and no model input. Parent still reaps direct child and observes group empty; failed startup never uses a no-spawn release after ProcessBuilder was attempted.

scheduling.owner: One bounded refill coordinator and one deadline watcher; no unbounded request or refill queue. Pool is lazy: first advisory demand starts a standby, and a consumed worker triggers at most one replacement after atomic slot admission.
scheduling.cold_miss: The sole active caller may wait for the current STARTING worker within the remaining startup and total request budgets, or synchronously initiate exactly one start when none exists. No bypass/fresh fallback hides cold costs. If capacity is UNKNOWN or full without a usable generation, return existing unavailable/busy behavior.
scheduling.idle: READY expires30s after readiness, retires and does not refill solely because it expired. New demand may refill after cleanup. Refill triggered by an actual consumption is charged to the same whole-stack resource budget and occurs during normal benchmark scheduling.
scheduling.deadline: Use monotonic elapsed time and clamp waits to remaining budget; recheck after awaited operations and immediately before handoff/publication. Startup5s includes image capture. The candidate10s budget starts at operation admission and is the deadline for accepting handoff and publishing success, including time spent in context, cold miss, validation, cleanup and final fences. Retirement/uncertain kernel cleanup can outlast it and must retain capacity; no theorem promises successful cleanup or a response within10s under a stalled OS. Deadline expiry suppresses success and requests retirement, never releases capacity. Existing fresh worker10s exchange remains unchanged. Add a context-gateway overload accepting remaining time for this candidate only; preserve the ordinary20s gateway behavior. FrameProcess may be factored for bounded waits without changing old callsite behavior. All new identity scans and image/refill CPU costs are measured.

implementation_map.backend_pool: Add encapsulated package-private ledger, cgroup ownership, image helper launcher, warm transport and advisory pool classes with documented methods<=30physical lines. No public request flag or environment-selected JVM options. Pool selection is a fixed trusted compile-time policy, disabled until selection.
implementation_map.worker_entrypoint: Add dedicated one-use warm entrypoint; factor DocumentWorkerMain only to share the same exact bounded decoder/engine/response path and preserve fresh behavior. Do not expose durable REVALIDATE to the warm path.
implementation_map.integration: DocumentQueries invokes an advisory adapter after existing context resolution. DocumentWorker and ProcessRunner reserve/release shared live-tree tokens only in enabled mode. Lifecycle shutdown retires all generations before releasing runtime ownership. Add candidate-only deadline/operation-binding overloads to DocumentGateway and DocumentValidationContext; preserve existing callers and closed SQL envelopes. The context permit is consumed, never cached or reused.
implementation_map.helper: Small trusted Python helper under scripts or installed package; isolated interpreter, fixed executable paths, no shell, bounded closed bootstrap schema, no DB/network/model access, no inherited credentials. Runtime executable identity is bound to candidate manifest. Pin exact helper-source SHA in the compiled trusted launcher and recheck it before each start; include interpreter/stdlib/native runtime identities in the experiment manifest. Use an isolated installed interpreter with fixed paths, not ambient Conda or inherited PYTHONPATH.
implementation_map.tests: Use actual bwrap/helper/cgroup path for integration, not a command-only launcher bypass. Test seams do not enable alternate production authority. Freeze runtime correspondence as finite tests/structural checks, never claim Lean proves the Java, Python, JVM or kernel.

formal_boundary: Only exact reachable-state propositions in WarmPool.lean are proved: two-slot reservation bound, single unassigned generation, single consumption, guarded CLEAN handoff, staging/cleanup/fence/publication order, sticky cancellation, nonrevival, exact generation release, and witness traces. Actual identity observations, descriptor seals, filesystem persistence, kernel containment, timers, SQL cleanup, Java correspondence and measured performance require independent runtime evidence and remain outside the model theorem.
selection: Keep DEFAULT unless every experiment.json safety, differential, resource, cold, sustained and original paired HTTP promotion requirement passes. Any unsupported cgroup/image feature blocks the candidate without weakening isolation. The prior Tier-1 KEEP_F0 evidence remains unchanged. Commercial release remains NO_GO and target-host acceptance OPEN.
